# Owned stream inputs

`scripts/generate-stream-fixtures.py` creates these small test inputs from project-owned byte patterns using Python's reference BZip2/LZMA implementations. `--check` checks reproducibility. Phrase inputs contain `abracadabra abracadabra\n` repeated six times. Empty members contain no bytes. `multiple.bz2` concatenates an empty and phrase member; `multiple.lz` concatenates phrase, empty and phrase members. The multiblock input contains 320,000 bytes defined by `(i * 73 ^ (i >> 8)) & 255` and uses BZip2 level 1.

TAR inputs contain one `hello.txt` with the phrase, represented as deterministic ustar with a zero timestamp. The LZMA Alone known-size vector patches only the eight-byte size field of the independent unknown-size stream, retaining its EOS marker. Lzip v1 framing follows the [author's format description](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-diaz-lzip/02/), using independently generated raw LZMA and Python's CRC32. This generator is not itself an independent Lzip interoperability result; actual external-reader results belong in the delivery issue. The `bad-header` inputs keep valid compression framing and a ustar marker, but deliberately change the first name byte without updating the TAR header checksum. They verify that identified TAR corruption cannot downgrade to ordinary-file success. No reference implementation code, user archives or execution evidence is stored here.
